results.name: PHP2Shell: Exploitation Attempts and Remediation Trends
results.description: Wiz Research has been monitoring exploitation attempts targeting two critical PHP vulnerabilities since their public disclosure on October 21, 2026. While no successful attacks have been observed in their telemetry, some private exploits have been shared that work against various targets. Telemetry shows a 67% decrease in exposed vulnerable machines and a 47.9% reduction in significantly affected organizations within one week. Observed exploitation attempts include tools using the PHP2Shell mechanism matching public proof-of-concepts, though none completed the full exploit chain. Challenges preventing successful exploitation include request-size limits, memory exhaustion failures, and difficulties with worker pinning across different PHP configurations. Additionally, some tools branded as PHP2Shell exploits actually relied on unrelated session poisoning techniques requiring separate local file inclusion vulnerabilities. results.name: Attackers Abuse ChatGPT Custom GPTs to Deliver RAT via ClickFix
results.description: Threat actors are exploiting ChatGPT Custom GPTs and Google Sites to deliver remote access trojans through a sophisticated multi-stage attack chain. The campaign uses sponsored Google search results to direct victims to attacker-created Custom GPTs that impersonate legitimate ChatGPT models. Victims are then redirected to a malicious Google Sites page presenting a fake CloudFlare CAPTCHA that deploys a ClickFix lure, tricking users into executing PowerShell commands. This initiates an eight-stage infection chain involving obfuscated scripts, malicious MSI installers, and DLL sideloading through legitimately signed Canon or Stardock executables. The payload establishes dual persistence mechanisms and deploys a full-featured RAT with capabilities including remote desktop access, credential harvesting from seventeen browsers, file management, and payload deployment. Huntress investigators responded to at least 40 related incidents with two confirmed Custom GPT-driven infections.

results.name: Node2Shell / HTTP2Shell Vulnerability May Allow RCE
results.description: An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Google's Brotli decoder, tracked as CVE-2026-111497 and known as Node2Shell or HTTP2Shell, affects Node.js and various other software packages. The critical flaw (CVSS 9.2) can be triggered when vulnerable processes decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data, potentially leading to crashes, memory disclosure, or remote code execution. The vulnerability impacts multiple runtimes including Node.js, Bun, Python, .NET, Envoy Proxy, and Java brotli4j. Exploitation can occur through both inbound malicious requests and outbound responses from compromised servers. Within 24 hours of disclosure, reconnaissance and exploitation attempts were observed from 20 source IP addresses across 402 events, with 40% involving reconnaissance and 60% exploitation attempts. Organizations should immediately patch vulnerable components and monitor for suspicious activity.

results.name: n0n Ransomware: Inside an AI-Assisted Extortion Operation
results.description: In September 2026, an exposed staging server revealed the complete operational workspace of a n0n ransomware operator, including breach tools, encryptor source code, extortion infrastructure, and an AI coding agent environment with over $7,000 in paid LLM API usage. The investigation identified at least 23 victim organizations across 14 countries spanning multiple sectors. Every documented compromise relied exclusively on weak or stolen credentials, with no vulnerability exploitation observed. The operation combines data exfiltration with either encryption or complete data destruction, including backup deletion. The operator leveraged an AI coding agent configured with 154 models to generate hundreds of attack scripts, demonstrating human-directed operations augmented by artificial intelligence. By October 2026, n0n had listed 93 victims with combined ransom demands totaling $283.7 million, using credential stuffing against FortiGate SSL-VPN devices, exposed cloud keys, and compromised management portals a...

results.name: PHP2Shell Weaponized After Japanese Real Estate Extortion
results.description: An exposed staging server at 96.126.130.81 revealed an operator's extortion campaign targeting Japanese real estate websites between October 9-11, 2026, followed by PHP2Shell exploitation tooling. The operator, using the handle kkkkevin777, compromised one Japanese real estate services company and pivoted to nearly 20 related sites through shared hosting credentials. Stolen data included 16,061 customer records with plaintext passwords, income details, and addresses. The operator deployed ransom pages with an October 11 deadline and pressured victims by threatening to expose customer data. PHP2Shell tooling arrived on October 21, ten days after the extortion wave, indicating the operator was preparing new capabilities. Additionally, databases and emails from a Taiwanese company were exfiltrated. The server contained weaponized PHP2Shell reproducers, web shells, beacon logs, and scripts for lateral movement, though no confirmed PHP2Shell exploitation against live targets was documented.

results.name: 68 GB Stolen From a Philippine Government Agency's Overseas-Employment Databases, Exposed by the Operator's Own Open Directory
results.description: An unidentified operator exfiltrated 68.837 GiB of database backups from a Philippine government agency managing overseas employment and migrant workers on 6 September 2026. The theft involved 27 SQL Server backups containing case-management systems including POEA and OFW variants. The operator inadvertently exposed their staging infrastructure via an open HTTP directory on a UpCloud VPS in Singapore, revealing a rebranded GodPotato privilege escalation tool (renamed Wrqsnx), PowerShell stagers, Impacket toolkit, and transfer logs. The payload leverages DCOM and RPC mechanisms to achieve SYSTEM-level access without exploiting vulnerabilities. Certificate analysis linked the compromised infrastructure to the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration portal farm. Initial access vectors and command-and-control channels remain unidentified, though tooling was delivered to agency portal hosts.

results.name: Managed for Malice: How Attackers Turn MDM into Remote Access
results.description: Threat actors are weaponizing legitimate mobile device management platforms, including Hexnode and Rippling, through social engineering techniques to establish unauthorized remote access to victim systems. Attackers use phishing emails with business-themed lures, such as proposals and meeting invitations, to trick users into enrolling devices or installing management agents. Once MDM access is established, adversaries leverage this trusted, privileged path to deploy unauthorized remote monitoring and management tools like ScreenConnect, which connect to attacker-controlled relays. The deployment chain typically follows a pattern: social engineering leading to MDM enrollment, followed by RMM installation and external relay connections. This technique demonstrates the challenge of distinguishing legitimate administrative tools from malicious use, as the MDM platforms themselves are not compromised but rather misused through deception.

results.name: False Protection, Emptied Accounts: The Seven Android Trojan Families Targeting Indian Banking Apps
results.description: Group-IB's Threat Intelligence team uncovered a sophisticated Android malware campaign systematically targeting India's financial services sector since July 2025, orchestrated by the financially-motivated threat cluster CyberDakait. The operation distributes seven distinct malware families through coordinated smishing and vishing campaigns, impersonating bank representatives to trick victims into installing malicious APKs. These trojans harvest sensitive banking credentials, credit card details, and outstanding balances through overlay attacks while simultaneously conducting cryptojacking using XMRig. The malicious applications are hosted on GitHub repositories to maintain legitimacy, with the initial APK functioning as a dropper for the main payload and cryptocurrency mining module. Analysis revealed at least 17,960 compromised devices with 7.6 million intercepted SMS messages, including OTPs and transaction notifications. results.name: Amazon Threat Intelligence identifies PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure in MadPot
results.description: Amazon Threat Intelligence discovered PHP2Shell exploitation attempts in MadPot honeypot telemetry on October 17, 2026, four days before the public disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The initial exploit originated from a commercial anonymization network, suggesting threat actor involvement during the embargo period. Multiple proof-of-concept exploits emerged on the disclosure date, with varied payloads and infrastructure indicating multiple actors. Following the embargo lift on October 21, 2026, exploitation became widespread within hours. This incident highlights two critical lessons: coordinated disclosure cannot guarantee zero-day protection, and AI-assisted analysis has dramatically shortened the time from patch release to working exploits, requiring organizations to measure patch timelines in hours rather than days.

results.name: Telerik UI Exploitation Leads to Webshell Install and Scanner Execution
results.description: Multiple attack campaigns exploiting CVE-2019-18935, a remote code execution vulnerability in unpatched Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX servers, have been identified. The first case involved exploiting the vulnerability to execute a reverse shell connecting to 206.82.6.22, attempting privilege escalation using Potato-family tools like SweetPotato, and installing a Godzilla-style memory-based web shell that operates within the w3wp.exe process without requiring separate ASPX files. The second case deployed a Rust-based scanner tool that searches for exposed WordPress installation pages across target systems and reports findings via Telegram. Both attacks targeted Windows IIS servers, enabling attackers to maintain persistent access, collect system information, and identify additional targets for future campaigns.
